open_points.subject: source-supplied timestamp normalization
open_points.text: “Times a source supplies … are kept as supplied: the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC …; their accepted forms and checks … are … carried to States 6–7.”
open_points.question: Which source timestamp forms are accepted, especially an offset-naive datetime, and how is each accepted form converted to offset-naive UTC without changing its instant?
options: Require an explicit UTC offset, convert to UTC, then remove the offset
Accept an offset-naive value and interpret it as UTC
Accept only values already expressed with UTC offset zero
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit offset, convert the instant to UTC, then store it without tzinfo.

witness.initial: No snapshot exists; the producer supplies approved_at as the offset-naive value 2026-11-08 10:00:00.
events: The portal decodes and stores approved_at.
outcomes: The portal interprets the value as UTC and stores 2026-11-08 10:00:00.
The portal rejects the publication because the value does not identify an instant.
witness.observer: The producer sees acceptance versus rejection, and later readers see whether the timestamp was stored.

open_points.subject: wall-clock read placement
open_points.text: “where in an operation its one clock read happens, are the accepted spec's, carried to States 6–7.”
open_points.question: At what exact point does each operation take its single wall-clock reading relative to request entry, authentication and expiry checks, external calls, validation, and the transaction?
options: At request or operation entry before other work
Immediately before the first current-time comparison
At an operation-specific point that must be named in its later contract
open_points.default_guess: Read immediately before the first current-time comparison and reuse that instant for the remainder of the operation.

witness.initial: A credential expires at instant T; a request arrives just before T but reaches its expiry check just after T.
events: A service principal sends a snapshot publication request.
The portal begins processing before T.
The portal performs the credential-expiry check after T.
outcomes: A reading taken at operation entry is before T, so the credential is usable and processing continues.
A reading taken at the expiry check is at or after T, so the request is refused as expired.
witness.observer: The service principal sees an accepted/classified attempt versus an authentication refusal with no import record.

open_points.subject: audit classification of an idempotent snapshot replay
open_points.text: “either changes no business state and is recorded as its own import result and `snapshot.import` audit”
open_points.question: What `AuditResult` and `reason_code` must the `snapshot.import` audit carry for an `idempotent_replay`?
open_points.default_guess: Record the idempotent replay as success with no reason code.

witness.initial: An accepted snapshot already exists for a key and fingerprint.
events: The same service principal republishes identical content.
The portal creates the required fresh idempotent-replay import result and snapshot.import audit.
outcomes: The audit records success with no reason code because the replay completed normally.
The audit records rejected with idempotent_replay as its reason because no new snapshot was accepted.
witness.observer: An audit consumer or invariant test sees different result and reason fields for the same replay.
